note: Re-judged 2026-11-08 (independent auditor) after 79e3205310 (LAC realm relay). writeICCNBody now takes an *iccnProxy, and a realm call's ICCN carries AVPs 26 to 33 and, toward a remote with a shared secret, a Random Vector (AVP 36) ahead of a hidden AVP 33 (iccn_proxy.go writeICCNProxyAVPs, writeAVPRandomVector). TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags still walks only writeICCNBody(buf, 64000, 1, nil), and its tag comments were narrowed to 'these writers'. FINDING (weak): RFC 2661 Section 4.4 forbids hiding the Random Vector ('This AVP MUST NOT be hidden (the H-bit MUST be 0)'), and Ze now emits one in every PAP realm ICCN toward a remote with a secret, next to the one AVP it hides (33, which Section 4.4.5 lets be hidden). The tagged walk never reaches that body, so a writer that set H on the Random Vector, or on Message Type, Tx Connect Speed or Framing Type in the proxy ICCN, leaves TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags green. TestWriteICCNBodyHiddenAVP33 does assert the Random Vector H=0 and that 33 is the only hidden AVP, but it is tagged RFC2661-4.3-1/4.3-3, not this row. Fix: walk the proxy ICCN in writtenBodies with AVP 33 exempted from the H check, or tag TestWriteICCNBodyHiddenAVP33 for this row. {single-polarity} still holds: skipHiddenAVP (avp.go) still refuses every hidden AVP on receipt. Prior judgement: Forbidden = an AVP whose definition forbids hiding emitted with H=1. message_rfc2661_test.go::TestRFC2661WrittenAVPFlags walks every AVP of every body Ze writes and fails on any H=1. Row carries single-polarity.
